newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal transporters oppose oil price hike.
newsitem.headline: Nepal transporters oppose oil price hike.

text.p: Nepali bus and truck owners on Monday threatened to raise fares if the state-owned Nepal Oil Corporation (NOC) does not withdraw a fuel price hike.
The NOC last week raised the price of petrol by 14.7 percent, diesel by 25 percent, kerosene by 15.7 percent and cooking gas by 60 percent.

"If the government does not withdraw its decision immediately, the federation will increase transport fares from 35 percent to 50 percent," the Nepal Transport Entrepreneurs' Federation (NTEF) said in a statement.
The NTEF, the largest transport operators' group in the country, said the increase in domestic oil prices came despite flat global crude prices.
The communist Unified Marxist-Leninist (UML) party, the dominant partner in the three party ruling coalition, has also protested against the price rises.
"The price rise is a breach of popular trust," said Pradeep Nepal, head of UML's local organisation panel.
A communist-backed students' union threatened to launch protest rallies if the increases were not revoked.
The NOC has a monopoly over the import and distribution of petroleum products in the Himalayan kingdom, and imports some 600,000 tonnes of petroleum products every year.
It had said imports were becoming more and more expensive and the price raise was needed to save the corporation from making a loss.
Members of the Consumers' Forum also staged a sit-in demonstration at the NOC office on Sunday in protest against the price increases.
